angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 487,686 km at 141.95 pc = 0.05 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 7.0448 +/- 0.0105 mas (same row, RUWE 1.07): 141.95 pc, no zero-point correction
radiusSource: Radius 0.701 +/- 0.017 solar radii from Hartman et al. 2009, the stellar radius of the default parameter set of HAT-P-12 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2009ApJ...706..785H/abstract): 487,686 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 0.733 +/- 0.018 solar masses from Hartman et al. 2009, the stellar mass of the default parameter set of HAT-P-12 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2009ApJ...706..785H/abstract); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 4650 +/- 60 K from Hartman et al. 2009, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of HAT-P-12 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2009ApJ...706..785H/abstract). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Hartman et al. 2009, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of HAT-P-12 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2009ApJ...706..785H/abstract)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/hat-p-12.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 4.612, rounded to two decimals

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, colored from the star's Gaia DR3 BP/RP spectrum (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
